questions.question: How do you use a key to read a map? Give an example.
questions.expected_answer: First read the title, then look at the key to learn what each symbol means. Then find each symbol on the map and use the key to understand it. For example, the key shows that a blue wiggly line is a stream, so a blue wiggly line on the map shows where the stream is.

questions.question: Why does a map of part of a town have more symbols than a map of a farm?
questions.expected_answer: A town has many more buildings and services, such as a hospital, police station, library, taxi rank and places of worship, packed close together, so more symbols are needed.

questions.question: List the steps for drawing your own map.
questions.expected_answer: Write a title. Draw the area as a plan view from above, big things first, each in the right place. Use simple symbols, the same symbol for the same kind of thing. Draw a key in a box in a corner with every symbol and its meaning. Add a north arrow. Check your map.
